Apple has updated the privacy policy of its Apple Store app to include terms related to an upcoming virtual shopping assistant. Details below.

Apple is expanding the application of artificial intelligence in its retail business

According to MacRumors, the Apple Store app and its privacy page have added a new section titled "Virtual Shopping Assistant," with the following content:

In other words, the Apple Store app will likely soon feature a chatbot function, providing personalised responses based on user data and helping users make purchasing decisions.

Apple stated that conversations between users and the assistant will have personally identifiable information removed before being shared with an unnamed partner to generate the assistant's responses, indicating that this experience is likely powered at least in part by a third-party company's model.

Conversation records will be retained within the app for users to review, while Apple will also store these records for business analytics purposes. Users can opt in or out through a new "Chat Improvements" setting, which controls whether conversations may be used to improve the virtual shopping assistant's performance.

Based on the wording of Apple's privacy policy, the virtual assistant may initially launch only in selected countries and regions, and is highly likely to debut in English-speaking markets before gradually expanding to more languages and regions.

This announcement comes months after Apple added an AI chatbot to its Sales Coach app. Sales Coach provides Apple retail partners with sales and technical support resources, allowing employees to use the chatbot via the "Ask" tab, where the system answers questions based on Apple's official training materials and documentation.

Additionally, Bloomberg previously reported that Apple has been testing a system called "Live Notes" in some retail stores, which uses AI to record, transcribe, and summarise conversations during Genius Bar support sessions, allowing employees to focus on serving customers without being distracted by taking notes.

To learn more about the Apple Store app and its privacy policy, please visit the link below.
